findings.statement: Adjudicated FAIL preserved: the r3 oracle report (exit 10) shows exactly one failing check anywhere — N7X_exchange on the three P-fixed SS states (sup_rel 4.91e-2 / 5.03e-2 / 5.36e-2) — while every physics-bearing check passes on all members, including N1/N2/N3 on the five asymmetric members under their caps (N3 max 5.09e-11 vs 1e-10, SB under 2.5e-10), N7X at fp level (max 7.68e-13), the certified interval residuals bracketing the float64 values within slack, M-INT-2 (1522656 containment checks, 0 containment and 0 identity failures, contraction ok), all five mutants killed with recorded margins plus a bitwise restoration canary, and the D-055 N8 anchors matched EXACTLY at all three SS states. The failure is a contract-design defect of the adjudicated D-054 S-B class (a relative metric applied to a degenerate observable): for P-fixed states the mu and tau logit rows are equal with a common slope, so for the four {mu,tau} distinct-elastic exchange events the Pauli affinity u3+u4-u1-u2 = (-1/s)(y3+y4-y_alpha-y_beta) vanishes identically by massless elastic energy conservation, leaving N7X to compare pure float64 cancellation noise against cancellation noise (rate magnitudes ~1e-34 at the diagonal node pair) — not a physics or implementation failure, since the same check passes at 2.3e-14..7.7e-13 on every member where the observable is nondegenerate. Permitted supersession scope per the D-054/D-055 precedent is exactly one change: restrict N7X gating to family members with distinct mu/tau state rows (the SA/SB blocks), with SS-state N7X values still computed and recorded non-gating alongside the degeneracy rationale; every other family member, threshold, formula, mutant, and interval tier must remain byte-identical in behaviour.
